subject: Aurelia Health - us-west-2 AZ latency spike and coordinated failover
messages:
From: Samantha Choa <samantha.choa@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:23 -0700
Subject: RE: Production errors / 5xx + latency - us-west-2

Hey Rachel,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and 502/504 spikes in us-west-2 beginning ~08:55 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 4.7% across our write-heavy endpoints. Throughput (rps) appears stable but tail latency is terrible for customer-facing APIs. Attached is a brief log snippet and a couple of Grafana screenshots.

We have customers in the middle of high-traffic runs and two sunk-in workflows are timing out. Can Redwood confirm whether there's an AZ issue or anything on your side that should trigger a cross-region failover? Please advise next steps — we need a short-term routing mitigation and an ETA for stabilization.

Attachments: aurelia_latency_log_snippet.txt, aurelia-kpi-screenshot.png

— Samantha Choa
Platform Ops, Aurelia Health
ops@aureliahealth.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:22:10 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RE: Production errors / 5xx + latency - us-west-2

Marissa / Aditya — looping you in. Aurelia is seeing a spike in 5xx and tail latency in us-west-2 (AZ boundaries look like az-2 is worst). Their chart shows latency and error rate rising sharply at ~08:55 PDT. They asked specifically about cross-region failover.

Ask: please confirm whether we have an automated routing fallback that can be triggered (canary / partial traffic) and what manual steps are required to move critical customers to eastus2. Need an estimate for how long the switch would take and impact on session affinity / KV caches.

I copied Vivek to keep CS/exec aware and Sean for any customer comms. I'm attaching the log snippet they sent. I'll keep Samantha on the thread for updates.

Attachments: aurelia_latency_log_snippet.txt

Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Choa <samantha.choa@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:30:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Production errors / 5xx + latency - us-west-2

Thanks Rachel — seeing the same telemetry in the Redwood control plane. us-west-2 AZ-2 shows elevated scheduler queue depth and higher GPU-side latency on a subset of instances. Docker host churn is low but a couple of worker pods are producing long GC pauses.

Immediate plan (short):
- Aditya: please trigger the regional routing playbook to start a controlled drain of affected AZ-2 nodes and activate cross-region steer of 20% -> eastus2 for affected model routes.
- Put an explicit session-affinity exemption for Aurelia's critical model routes (they are stateful on K/V cache) so we avoid cache-miss storms.
- Enable stricter circuit-breaker thresholds for 1 minute to avoid retry storms.

Impact notes: partial traffic shift should reduce tail latency for most customer requests within ~5-10 minutes, but some stateful requests may see a cold-KV miss stretch for a handful of sessions. We have a fallback to warm caches via snapshot seeding if needed.

Related runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-runbook-link
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2142

Marissa Cole
VP, Serving Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: Samantha Choa <samantha.choa@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:48:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Production errors / 5xx + latency - us-west-2

On Mon, May 14, 2028 at 09:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — seeing the same telemetry in the Redwood control plane. us-west-2 AZ-2 shows elevated scheduler queue depth and higher GPU-side latency on a subset of instances.

Initiated the routing playbook now:
- Started controlled drain of impacted AZ-2 worker pool (tag: us-west-2-az2-impacted).
- Flows: steering policy applied: affected model routes -> 20% traffic to eastus2, 80% remain but on healthy hosts in us-west-2.
- Session-affinity exemption added for aurelia-critical-route:v3 to preserve KV locality.
- Kicked off cache-warm snapshots to eastus2 for top 200 session keys (background job).

Planned next 30m checkpoints:
- 09:55 PDT: validate error-rate delta and tail latency across Aurelia routes.
- 10:20 PDT: escalate to 50% if no improvement.
- 10:45 PDT: if still degraded, we will propose full region failover for the impacted routes.

Attachments: routing-playbook.pdf, runbook-extract.txt

Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Choa <samantha.choa@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 12:45:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Production errors / 5xx + latency - us-west-2

Thanks team — appreciate the quick action and the clear checkpoints. Quick executive summary to pass upstream:

- Incident: sudden tail-latency and 502/504 spike impacting Aurelia Health customers in us-west-2 (AZ-2).
- Immediate mitigation: partial traffic steering (20% -> eastus2) and cache warm snapshots initiated; session-affinity exemption in place.
- Current impact: visible drop in tail-latency for sample routes; monitoring shows error-rate falling from 4.7% to ~1.1% after partial steering.
- Next steps: 10:20 checkpoint to consider increasing to 50%; 10:45 decision point for full regional failover if necessary.

I'll schedule a 15-minute exec bridge with Aurelia's CTO and our VP of Ops at 13:00 PDT to confirm communication and next steps. Rachel — please prepare a short customer note summarizing current state and expected timeline; Sean, hold on customer comms until we confirm stabilization or a full failover decision.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success (Acting)
Redwood Inference
